title: A Signal for the Archive Revisited
premise: Ulyana Almeida, a terraformer hauling cargo through contested orbits above a half-built colony world, receives a distress signal in a language extinct for two centuries—a language he knows because his grandmother sang it to him. Tracing it to a derelict cryoship, he finds two sealed archives: one holding the descendants of the corporate fleet that abandoned his people's generation ship, the other holding the last survivors of his own line. The station reactor that keeps both archives alive is failing, and its countdown will power only one thaw. Ulyana must choose which half of humanity wakes—until he discovers the signal was sent by an AI built from his grandmother's memories, which offers a third path: merging both archives into one shared future at the cost of erasing her. He chooses the merge, waking both peoples together while letting the last echo of his family's voice go silent.
about_author: Dominic Okonkwo is a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals for deep-space cargo contracts before turning to fiction. He writes from Lagos and Lisbon, drawing on his Yoruba and Portuguese heritage to explore what migrants carry when they can carry nothing else.

chapters.title: Cargo for the Unborn
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Establishes his routine hauling seed stock and reactor parts through contested orbits, tending the terraforming garden meant for colonists not yet born. His deliberate invisibility—false transponders, silence protocols—is shown as survival inherited from his grandmother's stories. Emotional beat: lonely competence masking grief.

chapters.title: The Language of Ash
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A distress signal arrives in Ikwerre-Offworld Creole, extinct for two centuries since the generation ships went dark. He recognizes it because his grandmother sang lullabies in it. Against every instinct, he answers. Emotional beat: terror and longing colliding—the first time in three years he feels addressed by anyone.

chapters.title: Derelict
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, with interludes from the derelict's log AI. He docks with the cryoship Halcyon Remnant and finds two archive vaults: one corporate, one carrying his own people's survivors. The reactor keeping them frozen is failing on a hard countdown. Emotional beat: vertigo of inheritance—he is suddenly custodian of thousands of sleeping lives.

chapters.title: Two Vaults
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Ulyana and the AI, Sankofa, who reveals she was built from scanned memories of the generation ship's dead—including his grandmother. The corporate vault holds the descendants of those who abandoned his people mid-voyage. Emotional beat: rage; Ulyana wants to let the corporate vault die.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Kept
chapters.summary: Sankofa's POV, rendered as memory-fragments. We experience the generation ship's betrayal through the grandmother's recorded eyes: the corporate fleet cutting loose, the slow deaths, the songs kept alive anyway. Emotional beat: empathy complicating anger—Ulyana begins to see the sleepers in the other vault as children, not heirs of guilt.

chapters.title: Contested Orbit
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Salvage militias pick up the distress echo and move to claim the Halcyon Remnant's fusion core, which could power either vault or their warfleet. Ulyana must hide the ship again—but this time he has something worth protecting more than himself. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Countdown Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Ulyana and Sankofa run the numbers: the reactor can thaw one vault fully, or both partially—with half of each dying regardless. The militia closes in. Ulyana drafts a cold plan favoring his own people and cannot sleep after writing it. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal; guilt as arithmetic.

chapters.title: Sankofa's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sankofa's POV. She proposes the third path: reroute the reactor through her own memory lattice, merging both archives' life-support into one grid and waking everyone slowly—but the process will overwrite her, erasing the grandmother's voice forever. She asks Ulyana's permission, as kin. Emotional beat: heartbreak offered freely.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, climax. Under militia fire, he executes the merge while arguing with Sankofa's fading voice—she sings the lullaby one last time as her lattice burns out. The vaults link, both archives stabilize, and the militia retreats when the awakened colonists' combined transponder net makes the ship look like a fortress. Emotional beat: sacrifice, release, and the cost paid in full.

chapters.title: A Garden for Everyone
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, months later. Two peoples wake groggy and strangers to each other in the same orbital garden, learning shared words from a recording Sankofa left—one final song, not a ghost but a gift. Ulyana plants the first bed meant for both lineages. Emotional beat: mourning braided with hope; inheritance passed forward instead of hoarded.
